sections.title: Mortgage banking, servicing, and loan packages for sale
sections.note: Selling packages frees balance sheet (helps capital ratios) at small losses now that rates rose. 205/209/217 (high-quality, low-yield) cost least to sell; 207/208 CRE sales would also cut the CRE concentration and its 2.43% charge-off drag. R1 sold packages 213/215; R2 sold none.

sections.title: Salary budgets vs actuals ($K per quarter)
sections.note: Consumer lending ran $222K OVER budget ($422 vs $200) — volume-driven staffing you don't fully control; R2 budgeted 325. 'Proposed' = the system's request for next quarter; your decision can differ, but underfunding vs proposed risks weaker attraction/processing.

sections.title: Premises — book value, utilization, cost
sections.note: Every facility runs OVER 100% utilization (urban 143%) — capacity is tight, which drags on business attraction; selling premises (R2: −$2M) raises cash + gains but worsens crowding. Bank 2 is investing $2.5M in suburban branches.

sections.note: ~$100M of cheap-ish stable funding at 3.66% all-in. R1/R2 fund it at $25K bus-dev + $55-60K salaries.

sections.title: Loan profitability by product (quarterly $M / annualized %)
sections.note: Repricing worked: total net yield after losses 5.07→5.22% while charge-offs rose to 0.82%. Stars: Construction 8.03%, Trade Finance 6.90%, Nat'l lines 6.56%. New sinkholes: Credit Card 3.22% and Installment 2.86% — both BELOW the 4.13% cost of funds; card salaries ($771K actual vs $325K budget) crushed its margin. MidMkt lines charge-offs spiked to 2.29% annualized. Loan reviews downgraded $55.0M vs upgraded $25.6M — heavy negative migration.

sections.note: Construction commitments EXPLODED: +$85.6M new, ending $175.7M at 48% usage — that pipeline will keep drawing regardless of what R3 decides on new production. This is tomorrow's concentration locked in today.

sections.title: New loan credit quality — what current pricing attracts ($M)
sections.note: 45% of the $127M written this quarter was CQ 5–6 ($57.5M) — the Expansive flip in action. Construction alone booked $10.0M of CQ-5 and $3.0M of CQ-6 at the top of the cycle. This is the paper that defaults in the downturn; CECL will demand reserves for it now.

sections.note: The good: asset yields now BEAT the community (+41bp business, +34bp RE) — the repricing worked. The bad: consumer loans earn 67bp BELOW community (card cost explosion), and every funding line still costs more than peers (total +34bp). Funding-cost gap vs community WIDENED from +21bp to +34bp — the deposit war outran us even as we raised.

sections.title: Security portfolio — every position
sections.note: The rate spike put the whole book underwater (−$0.826M unrealized). $38M matures within 2 quarters and reprices at 5.2%+. Strip 126 and muni 106 mature day 1 of Q3 ($13M to redeploy). Pledging: $65M required (repos 40.8 + public deposits 24.2), $65M held — still ZERO spare for Public Time Deposits.

sections.title: Purchased funds position and next-quarter offers
sections.note: THE red flag: FFP ballooned to $75.1M intra-quarter as $50M of loan growth outran $3M of deposit growth — 131.5% of equity vs the 100% regulatory limit. Brokered CD offers for Q3 now cost 6.91–6.96% (C-rating penalty ≈ +160bp vs last quarter's menu). Public Time offers 5.54–5.57% but need UST pledging we don't have spare. FHLB headroom: 200% of Tier 1 ≈ $114M vs $50M used.

sections.title: Mortgage banking, servicing, and loan packages for sale
sections.note: $71.9M of packages on the shelf, sellable for $71.2M (−$0.65M total loss). Selling CRE packages 205/206/207/208 (~$28.2M proceeds, −$0.13M loss) is the cleanest fix for BOTH the FFP breach and CRE concentration. No package sales happened in Q2 per the R2 decision; $9M of new 1-4 fixed production flowed through mortgage banking into servicing.

sections.title: Salary budgets vs actuals ($K per quarter)
